internal.title: Incident Summary: Checkout Service Elevated Error Rate Due to Payment Service Error Injection
internal.body:
On 2026-11-08 at 11:07 UTC, the checkout service experienced a high error rate (9.5%) and elevated p95 latency (400 ms). Investigation identified a recent feature flag change in the payment service ('paymentFailure') that injected errors, causing knock-on failures in checkout. CPU and memory metrics were normal, ruling out resource exhaustion or memory leaks.

The flag was disabled at 11:27 UTC following approval, leading to rapid recovery and normalization of error rates in checkout. The incident was resolved without further impact.

Key timeline:
- 11:07:57: Alert received for high error rate in checkout
- 11:27:40: Diagnosis confirmed error injection in payment service
- 11:27:46: Flag disabled and recovery verified

Action items include reviewing feature flag deployment processes to prevent similar incidents.

external.title: Some checkouts failed due to payment service issue
external.body: Between 11:07 and 11:27 UTC on 2026-11-08, some customers experienced issues completing checkout due to a problem in the payment service. The issue was identified and resolved promptly, and normal service was restored. We apologize for any inconvenience caused.

output.impact: Some customers were unable to complete checkout during the incident window, experiencing errors and delays.
output.root_cause: A feature flag ('paymentFailure') in the payment service was enabled, injecting errors that caused elevated error rates and latency in the checkout service.
output.resolution: The problematic feature flag was disabled following diagnosis and approval, leading to recovery and normalization of service metrics.

lessons.lesson: Feature flag changes can introduce error injections that propagate to dependent services; thorough validation and staged rollouts are critical.
lessons.applies_when: When a feature flag injects errors causing downstream service failures.

action_items: Review and improve feature flag deployment and rollback procedures.
Enhance monitoring to detect error injections from feature flags earlier.
